chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and al-Razzaz, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, who said:

Indeed, Ibn Shubrumah said, 'Divorce is for the man.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'Divorce is for the women,' and the clarification of that is that the slave may have a free woman under him, so her divorce is three, and the free man may have a slave girl under him, so her divorce is two divorces.
ai.seo_question: How many divorces are valid for a slave woman married to a free man according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the jurisprudential principle that the number of revocable divorces (talaq) is determined by the status of the wife rather than the husband, a ruling derived from the analogy of a slave man marrying a free woman. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that just as a slave man has three divorces for his free wife, a free man has only two for his slave wife, reflecting the specific legal capacities in mixed-status unions. This distinction highlights the nuanced application of fiqh rules regarding social hierarchy and marital rights in early Shia jurisprudence.
